Hi Michael — Ben here (cc: Grace & Monica). Below is a compact technical packet that addresses the items you flagged. I attached a topology diagram (redwood_deployment_topology_v2.png) and an extractable attack-path matrix (ctb_attackpath_matrix.csv). If you want, we can walk these on a call and I can share a live view of our console and flow logs.

Topology summary (hosted vs private control plane)
- Hosted production (typical): customer requests land in a regional ingress tier, routed to an inference fabric spanning GPU pools. Control plane (tenant metadata, routing, model registry) runs in a logically separate VPC/subnet with no direct customer data egress; control-plane-heartbeat uses a dedicated management channel and mutual TLS to serving nodes.
- Private / VPC-connected deployment: control plane can be private to customer (private control plane option) and hosted connectors are replaced with an agent; customer traffic remains inside their transit network. Both modes preserve the same logical isolation model.

Isolation model (how tenants are partitioned)
- Tenant affinity: inference work is scheduled to tenant-scoped GPU pools. Tenants can pin to dedicated pools (Reserved/Dedicated) or run on shared pools that enforce namespace isolation.
- Memory/KV separation: KV caches are namespace-tagged with per-tenant encryption keys. We apply prefix-aware KV eviction and strict TTLs to avoid cross-tenant residue; encrypted cache keys are derived per-tenant and rotated daily by default.
- Process and kernel isolation: serving runtime launches model workers in distinct cgroups and leverages kernel namespace isolation for filesystem and IPC. We run a hardened sandbox for model execution with seccomp filters and runtime observability hooks.
- Data-at-rest: model artifacts and customer inputs are stored in encrypted object stores. Artifacts are signed (Sigstore-compatible) at ingestion and validated at load time; service rejects unsigned/unaltered artifacts.

Egress, peering, and network controls
- No direct customer egress from control plane to customer networks. Serving nodes egress through managed egress gateways with per-tenant NAT mapping when required; all egress is logged to flow logs with tenant IDs.
- VPC peering and private endpoints: private deployments support VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, or transit/router models. We implement route tables to limit what subnets can talk to external endpoints.
- Bastion/access: we use ephemeral credential brokers (no persistent bastions) for operator SSH access; session recordings and time-limited certs are enforced.

Model-serving continuity & fallback behavior
- Canary and fallback: rollout policies are model-version aware. If a serving pool degrades, requests are routed to compatible quantized variants pinned by policy; data never leaves the destination tenant context during fallback.
- Soft-fail circuit breaker: to avoid noisy neighbor or cold-start amplification we implement a tenant soft-fail circuit breaker — above configurable latency or error thresholds (default: p95 latency 300ms, error rate 1.0%) traffic is rate-limited and short-circuited to cached responses or a lower-cost quantized model.

Threat model highlights & prioritized attack paths (see attached CSV for matrix)
- Attack path A: Credential compromise -> control-plane token misuse. Mitigation: short-lived tokens (5m refresh), mTLS, HSM-backed KMS, and anomalous flow detection with automated token revocation.
- Attack path B: Cross-tenant inference leakage via KV/cache. Mitigation: per-tenant encrypted keys, prefix-aware eviction, and periodic cache scrub cycles; evidence: cache-scrub logs available via syslog/CloudWatch export for auditing.
- Attack path C: Supply-chain/model poisoning. Mitigation: artifact signing at ingestion, build provenance stored in immutable registry, runtime integrity checks. We also run offline model-evals and divergence monitors tied to Canary rollouts.

Operational evidence & controls we can provide
- Flow logs with tenant tags (13 months retention configurable), audit trail of control-plane actions (immutable write-ahead audit log), and SOC-2 type II report excerpts on request.
- We can produce a focused evidence packet: network ACL excerpts, flow log samples, signed model artifact sample, and a redacted audit timeline.

Attachments included in this reply: redwood_deployment_topology_v2.png (diagram), ctb_attackpath_matrix.csv (prioritized paths + mitigations).

If you want specific packet formats to fit your procurement spreadsheet, let me know which tabs to populate and I’ll export the fields directly into cobalttrust_rfi.xlsx.

Best,
